title: Design Partner Pilot Plan — Private VPC Terraform Modules (Alpha)
content:
Purpose
This doc defines the design partner pilot plan for the “VPC Terraform modules (alpha)” effort. The goal is to validate Redwood-validated defaults for AWS VPC-based private deployments, reduce variability in customer networking setups, and harden a repeatable deployment + validation path that Solutions Engineering (SE) and Professional Services (PS) can use in POCs.

Pilot outcomes we need:
- Validate the Terraform module interfaces and defaults against 2 real customer network environments.
- Validate installer preflight behavior (endpoints/DNS/IAM prerequisites) against what the modules create.
- Produce field-ready artifacts: example tfvars, a deployment guide, and a support playbook for common failure modes.

Scope (pilot)
In scope:
- AWS VPC networking + foundational infra created via redwood-terraform alpha modules:
  - VPC/subnet layout (public/private), route tables, NAT strategy
  - VPC endpoints (ECR, S3, STS, CloudWatch Logs, etc.) + private DNS options
  - Flow logs with customer-selectable destinations (CloudWatch Logs or S3)
  - Opinionated security group patterns for cluster ingress/egress
  - IAM scaffolding for installer execution role with permission boundary support
  - Optional VPN/DX placeholders/outputs (integration hooks; customer-owned connectivity implementation)
- Integration with Redwood Private installer (preflight checks; handoff from Terraform outputs to installer inputs)

Not in scope:
- Full end-to-end app install automation inside Terraform (installer/Helm covers cluster/app)
- Multi-cloud parity (GCP/Azure beyond stubs)
- Deep bespoke network topologies (we will document extension points/anti-patterns instead)

Design partners
We are targeting 2 design partners in the alpha window. Names are placeholders here; final confirmation tracked in PM-913.

1) Acme Bank (regulated, strict audit/logging)
- Motivators: SIEM export requirements, data residency, strict egress controls.
- Expected network posture: no public ingress, restricted egress, heavy endpoint usage, security review gating.
- Primary validation focus: endpoints + DNS behavior, flow logs destination/retention defaults, IAM boundaries.

2) Northstar Healthcare (POC speed + strict egress; on-prem future)
- Motivators: move quickly to POC while maintaining guardrails; expects on-prem trajectory later.
- Expected network posture: private subnets, egress via approved paths (NAT/proxy), requirements around DNS/TLS.
- Primary validation focus: minimum viable inputs, operability of defaults, and deployment guide clarity.

Assumptions and prerequisites
Customer-side assumptions (must be explicit during kickoff):
- AWS account(s) available with ability to create VPC, subnets, endpoints, NAT, security groups, IAM roles/policies.
- A target region and approved CIDR range(s) are decided.
- Customer will provide or approve log destination approach (CloudWatch Logs in their account OR S3 in their account). For alpha, Redwood does not own customer log buckets.
- Any VPN/Direct Connect is customer-managed; we only provide routing hooks/outputs.
- For EKS-based reference architecture: customer either uses existing EKS patterns or is open to Redwood Private installer constraints (private subnets, DNS resolution, outbound access to required AWS services).

Redwood-side prerequisites:
- A pinned alpha module version per pilot to reduce churn during their evaluation window.
- A named channel for real-time support (see Comms plan).
- A single accountable Redwood technical lead per pilot.

Environments / topology to validate
Each partner pilot should cover at least 2 environments to catch lifecycle issues (fresh create vs iterative updates).

Target minimum environments per partner:
- Env A: “Dev/Sandbox” (fresh VPC build)
  - Terraform apply from scratch
  - Installer preflight + install
  - Tear-down and re-create once to test idempotency and docs accuracy
- Env B: “Stage/POC” (longer-lived)
  - Terraform upgrades (pin -> bump patch/minor once)
  - Add one realistic customization (e.g., additional CIDR, additional endpoint policy, custom flow log destination)
  - Runbook: plan review + drift handling basics

Optional environment (if partner can support):
- Env C: “Prod-like” (change control)
  - Only if partner already has change management in place
  - We use it to validate that “least privilege + auditability” defaults pass their internal review

Success criteria
We will consider the pilot successful when all of the following are true (per partner unless noted):

Technical success metrics
- Deployment time-to-first-successful-install:
  - Dev/Sandbox: <= 1 business day from kickoff to first successful installer run (excluding partner internal approvals)
  - Stage/POC: <= 3 business days (excluding approvals)
- Installer preflight:
  - Clear pass/fail on required endpoints + private DNS behavior
  - If failing, error messages point to actionable remediation (module inputs + AWS console/CLI checks)
- No critical security regressions:
  - No unintended public ingress exposure by default
  - Egress defaults are documented; any public egress is explicit and opt-in (or clearly identified if unavoidable for their workload)
  - IAM: installer execution role permissions meet “least privilege scaffolding” intent and support permission boundaries
- Logging and auditability:
  - VPC Flow Logs enabled by default in pilot configs, with an approved destination
  - Retention and ownership are explicitly defined and accepted by partner (no ambiguity)

Product/UX success metrics
- Module interface “learnability”:
  - Partner can identify the minimal required variables and understands extension points
  - Any required overrides are captured as docs improvements or module changes (not tribal knowledge)
- Day-2 operations:
  - Partner can run terraform plan/apply with a checklist, and can safely rollback or pin versions
  - We capture at least 5 “gotchas” and convert them into docs/runbook items

Organizational success metrics
- SE/PS can reuse the artifacts (example tfvars + deployment guide) with minimal Eng involvement for the next 2 pilots.

Timeline (proposed)
Note: dates are illustrative; actual dates will follow partner availability and approvals.

Week 0: Prep (internal)
- Lock pilot module version (tag) + example config baseline.
- Confirm internal on-call rotation for pilot hours.
- Ensure installer preflight checks aligned with module defaults.

Week 1: Kickoff + Architecture alignment
- 60–90 min kickoff with partner platform/network/security leads.
- Confirm CIDR, region, DNS requirements, endpoint policy stance, logging destination, and egress approach.
- Document any constraints that push us off the supported topology.

Week 2: Dev/Sandbox build
- Partner applies Terraform in dev/sandbox.
- Redwood supports debug for:
  - VPC endpoint coverage (ECR/ECR DKR/S3/STS/CloudWatch Logs)
  - Private DNS flags and resolver settings
  - NAT/route table associations
  - Security group rules for installer/cluster components
- Run installer preflight + install.

Week 3: Stage/POC + docs hardening
- Apply to stage/POC.
- Perform one upgrade iteration (patch/minor bump) with a plan review checklist.
- Capture runbook notes and convert to:
  - Known issues + mitigations
  - “Validated defaults” statement
  - Extension points (what is safe to modify)

Week 4: Closeout + release readiness
- Pilot retrospective with partner.
- Produce a summary: what worked, what changed, what’s deferred.
- Confirm partner is comfortable being a design partner reference (internal only) and whether any sanitized artifacts can be shared.

Roles & responsibilities (RACI-style)
Accountable (A)
- Product (A): Vivek Kulkarni — scope, trade-offs, alpha commitments, prioritization.
- Infra Eng (A): Irene Choi — module technical direction, merge/release decisions.

Responsible (R)
- Networking module (R): Victor Alvarez — VPC/subnets/routing/NAT/endpoints defaults; troubleshooting.
- Terraform implementation (R): Bruno Silva — module changes, example tfvars updates, CI signal.
- Field execution lead (R): Markus Klein — customer coordination, pilot execution logistics, success criteria tracking.
- Pilot customer success (R): Rachel Kim — meeting cadence, action item tracking, escalations, postmortems.
- Deployment guide (R): Kira Thompson — step-by-step guide updates based on pilot feedback.

Consulted (C)
- Security/Compliance PM review (C): Naomi Feldman — posture statements, audit/log defaults.
- Security Eng (C): Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei — IAM boundaries, SIEM/log integration patterns.
- SRE (C): Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes — operational guardrails, runbook alignment.
- Regulated/on-prem requirements (C): Fatima Noor — industry constraints, forward compatibility.

Informed (I)
- Docs program (I): Elliot Price — labeling alpha vs GA, docs site alignment.
- Reference architecture review (I): Simran Kaur — architecture consistency checks.

Workstreams and deliverables per partner
For each partner, we will maintain a lightweight checklist:

A) Terraform deliverables
- [ ] Repo layout agreed (partner repo vs Redwood template)
- [ ] tfvars for dev/sandbox created
- [ ] tfvars for stage/POC created
- [ ] Version pinning in place (e.g., module version tags)
- [ ] Outputs wired for installer consumption (subnet IDs, endpoint flags, log destinations, etc.)

B) Validation deliverables
- [ ] CI/validation steps run (fmt/validate/tflint/checkov or partner equivalent)
- [ ] Integration test expectations communicated (what Redwood CI covers vs what partner will run)
- [ ] Installer preflight results captured (pass/fail + fixes)

C) Docs/runbook deliverables
- [ ] “Known issues” section updated (DNS, endpoints, NAT, SG)
- [ ] “Supported topologies + extension points” updated
- [ ] Upgrade/rollback procedure trialed once

Risk list (with mitigations)
1) Endpoint/DNS misconfiguration blocks installs (common)
- Symptoms: image pull failures, intermittent service resolution.
- Mitigation: installer preflight gating; docs include required endpoints and private DNS flags; include resolver setting checks during kickoff.

2) Strict egress policies conflict with defaults
- Mitigation: document egress model explicitly; provide private endpoints as default; make NAT/public egress behavior explicit. Identify where proxies are required and how to integrate.

3) IAM permission boundaries differ by enterprise org patterns
- Mitigation: keep IAM scaffold minimal; support boundary ARN as an input; provide a “required actions” checklist if customer uses centralized IAM.

4) Logging destination ownership and retention is unclear
- Mitigation: force explicit destination selection in pilot configs; provide suggested retention ranges; include SIEM hook patterns in appendix.

5) Change management delays (security/procurement) compress pilot feedback window
- Mitigation: front-load security questions in kickoff; keep Env A lightweight; agree on decision points and fallback to “dev only” validation if stage is blocked.

6) Module churn during alpha causes partner fatigue
- Mitigation: pin versions per partner; only ship patch-level changes unless explicitly approved; maintain a shared “pilot exceptions” log.

7) Cost/time of iterative applies (NAT gateways, endpoints) surprises partner
- Mitigation: provide a cost note for dev/sandbox; recommend enabling/limiting certain features by environment; ensure teardown guidance is clear.

Comms plan
Channels
- Dedicated Slack channel per partner (internal):
  - #pilot-acmebank-private-vpc (example)
  - #pilot-northstar-private-vpc (example)
- Shared internal channel for cross-pilot learnings: #eng-private-vpc-modules-alpha

Cadence
- Weekly 30-min pilot check-in with partner (SE lead + Eng lead + customer platform owner)
- Twice-weekly internal 15-min standup during Weeks 2–3 (pilot execution window)
- Async updates: short written status update after each major milestone (kickoff, dev success, stage success, upgrade trial)

Artifacts & documentation
- Single “Pilot packet” per partner (shared securely):
  - module versions + changelog notes relevant to the pilot
  - example directory layout and tfvars
  - deployment guide link
  - support escalation steps

Escalation policy
- Severity 1 (pilot blocked > 24h): route to Irene Choi + Victor Alvarez; notify Vivek Kulkarni; capture incident notes.
- Severity 2 (workaround exists): track in Linear under ENG-4821 epic and update docs within 48h.

Notes / open questions
- Confirm final design partner list + timeline (PM-913).
- Decide whether we run heavy integration tests per PR vs nightly during pilot window (cost vs confidence).
- Decide what sanitized configs we can safely share as “example tfvars” without leaking partner topology details.
- Confirm which DNS resolver settings we can safely recommend as default without overfitting to one partner environment.
